simple.meaning: שָׁרַשׁ (shârash) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “to root , i.e. strike into the soil , or (by implication) to pluck from it.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 8 times across Job, Psalms, Isaiah, Jeremiah, beginning at Job 5:3. Its contexts include kingship, mountain, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׁרַשׁ (H8327).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.

definitions.short: to root , i.e. strike into the soil , or (by implication) to pluck from it
definitions.full: H8327. sharash [ שָׁרַשׁ ] verb denominative Pi`el = deal with the roots ; — 1 root up, out : Perfect 3masculine singular suffix consecutive וְשֵׁרֶשְׁךָ Psa 52:7 he shall root thee up from ( מִן ) the land of the living; of fire (burn) roots, root : Imperfect 3feminine singular בְּ תְּשָׁרֵשׁ Job 31:12 fore (figurative) roots at all my increase. Pu`al Imperfect 3masculine plural יְשֹׁרָשׁוּ Job 31:8 be rooted up (of produce). 2. Po`el take root , establish oneself firmly: Perfect 3masculine singular בָּאָרֶץ שֹׁרֵשׁ גִּזְעָם Isa 40:24 (figurative of princes, etc.). Po`al id.: Perfect 3masculine plural שֹׁרָֹשׁוּ Jer 12:2 (figurative of wicked). Hiph`il id.: Imperfect 3masculine singular יַשְׁרֵשׁ Isa 27:6 (figurative of Israel); 3 feminine singular וַתַּשְׁרֵשׁ Psa 80:10 ( id. ; with accusative of congnate meaning with verb); Participle מַשְׁרִי Job 5:3 (figurative of person).

occurrences.englishText: I have seen the foolish taking root,
then let me sow, and let another eat.
for it is a fire that consumes to destruction,
“Behold, this is the man who didn’t make God his strength,
The mountains were covered with its shadow.
In days to come, Jacob will take root. Israel will blossom and bud. They will fill the surface of the world with fruit.
You have planted them. Yes, they have taken root.
